_source: Clinical haematology / biochemistry pattern recognition — BSH / NICE / WHO

patterns.name: Iron Deficiency Anaemia
patterns.criteria: Low Hb + Low MCV (<80 fL) + Low ferritin (<13 µg/L female, <30 µg/L male)
further_investigations: Serum iron + TIBC + ferritin if not done
Investigate cause: menorrhagia screen, GI endoscopy if male/>50F
patterns.management: Ferrous sulfate 200mg TDS × 3 months after Hb normalises. Treat underlying cause.

patterns.name: Anaemia of Chronic Disease
patterns.criteria: Low-normal Hb + Normal or raised MCV + Raised ferritin + Normal/Low serum iron + Low TIBC
patterns.management: Treat underlying disease. Iron supplementation only if concurrent IDA confirmed.

patterns.name: Megaloblastic Anaemia (B12 / Folate Deficiency)
patterns.criteria: Low Hb + High MCV (>100 fL) + Low B12 (<180 pmol/L) or Low folate
further_investigations: Intrinsic factor antibody if PA suspected
patterns.management: B12 deficiency: IM hydroxocobalamin or oral cyanocobalamin 1mg/day. Folate: folic acid 5mg/day × 4 months.

patterns.name: Atherogenic Dyslipidaemia (Metabolic Syndrome Pattern)
patterns.criteria: High TG (>1.7 mmol/L) + Low HDL + Normal/mildly raised LDL + High TC:HDL ratio
patterns.management: Intensive lifestyle modification. Statin if CVD risk ≥10% (NICE NG238). Fenofibrate if TG >5.6.

patterns.name: Possible Familial Hypercholesterolaemia
patterns.criteria: LDL ≥4.9 mmol/L (≥190 mg/dL)
further_investigations: Simon Broome / Dutch Lipid Clinic score
patterns.management: Classify as VERY HIGH CVD RISK regardless of calculator. High-intensity statin. Lipid clinic referral.

patterns.name: Metabolic Syndrome
patterns.criteria: ≥3 of: Central obesity (waist M>90cm/F>80cm SA) + Fasting glucose ≥5.6 mmol/L or known DM + TG ≥1.7 mmol/L + HDL low (M<1.0/F<1.2) + BP ≥130/85 or on antihypertensives
patterns.management: Intensive lifestyle: Mediterranean diet + ≥250 min/week exercise + weight loss ≥5%. Address each component individually.

patterns.name: Poorly Controlled Type 2 Diabetes
patterns.criteria: HbA1c >58 mmol/mol (>7.5%) on treatment
patterns.management: Intensify therapy: optimise metformin, add SGLT2i (if CVD/CKD) or GLP-1 RA or DPP4i. HbA1c target ≤53 mmol/mol.

patterns.name: Pre-diabetes
patterns.criteria: HbA1c 42–47 mmol/mol or fasting glucose 5.6–6.9 mmol/L
patterns.management: Intensive lifestyle: Mediterranean diet + ≥150 min/week exercise + weight loss if overweight (SA BMI ≥23). Recheck HbA1c 6-monthly.

patterns.name: Chronic Kidney Disease
patterns.criteria: eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73m² on ≥2 occasions ≥3 months apart, or uACR ≥3 mg/mmol
patterns.management: BP <130/80 with ACEi/ARB if proteinuria. Avoid NSAIDs, nephrotoxins. CKD G4+ → nephrology referral.

patterns.name: Hypothyroidism
patterns.criteria: High TSH (>4.0 mIU/L) + Low free T4
patterns.management: Levothyroxine: start 50–100 mcg/day. Titrate to TSH 0.5–2.5. Recheck TFT in 6 weeks.

patterns.name: Subclinical Hypothyroidism
patterns.criteria: TSH 4–10 mIU/L + Normal free T4
patterns.management: Treat if TSH >10 or symptomatic. Observe and repeat if TSH 4–10 asymptomatic.

patterns.name: Hyperthyroidism
patterns.criteria: Low TSH (<0.4 mIU/L) + High free T4 or free T3
patterns.management: Refer endocrinology. Carbimazole or PTU. Beta-blocker for symptom relief.

patterns.name: Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease / MASLD
patterns.criteria: Elevated ALT/AST (1.5–3×ULN) + No excess alcohol + Metabolic risk factors
patterns.management: Weight loss ≥7% body weight. Mediterranean diet. Treat metabolic syndrome. Restrict alcohol. Hepatology referral if fibrosis suspected.

patterns.name: Acute Hepatocellular Injury
patterns.criteria: ALT >3×ULN (>168 U/L male, >135 U/L female) — acute pattern
further_investigations: Viral hepatitis serology (HBsAg, anti-HCV, HAV IgM, HEV IgM)
Review all medications including herbals and supplements
patterns.management: Stop potentially causative drugs. Hepatology referral if ALT >3×ULN persistent or >10×ULN.

patterns.name: Vitamin D Deficiency
patterns.criteria: 25-OH Vitamin D <50 nmol/L
patterns.management: Deficiency (<25 nmol/L): loading dose regimen (colecalciferol 300,000 IU total). Insufficiency (25–50): 1000–2000 IU/day maintenance.
patterns.source: NICE PH56; SACN Vitamin D report

patterns.name: Hyperuricaemia / Gout Risk
patterns.criteria: Uric acid >0.45 mmol/L (male) or >0.36 mmol/L (female)
patterns.management: Acute gout: NSAIDs or colchicine or corticosteroid. Chronic: allopurinol (target urate <0.36 mmol/L). Lifestyle: reduce red meat, beer, fructose.

patterns.name: Hypercalcaemia
patterns.criteria: Corrected calcium >2.60 mmol/L
further_investigations: Chest X-ray / CT if malignancy suspected
patterns.management: Mild (2.6–3.0): monitor. Moderate-severe: IV fluids, bisphosphonate if malignancy. Refer endocrinology/oncology.

patterns.name: Hyponatraemia
patterns.criteria: Sodium <136 mmol/L
patterns.management: Treat underlying cause. Max correction rate 10 mmol/L in first 24h (osmotic demyelination risk). Severe symptomatic: endocrinology/nephrology input.

patterns.name: Polycythaemia
patterns.criteria: Haemoglobin >20 g/dL or haematocrit >0.52 (male) / >0.48 (female)
supporting: Raised WBC and platelets (if primary PV)
patterns.management: Haematology referral. Venesection if PV. Treat cause if secondary.

patterns.name: Neutropenia
patterns.criteria: Neutrophils <1.8 × 10⁹/L
further_investigations: Bone marrow biopsy if persistent severe
patterns.management: Severe neutropenia (<0.5): reverse barrier nursing. Review all medications. Haematology referral if persistent or unexplained.

patterns.name: Thrombocytopenia
patterns.criteria: Platelets <150 × 10⁹/L
patterns.management: Platelets <50 with bleeding: urgent haematology. Mild (100–150): observe and repeat. Haematology referral if <80 or symptomatic.

patterns.name: DKA / Hyperglycaemic Crisis Risk
patterns.criteria: Glucose >14 mmol/L + suspect ketonaemia/ketonuria
patterns.management: EMERGENCY: Hospital admission. IV fluids + IV insulin infusion + electrolyte monitoring.

patterns.name: Elevated Troponin — Myocardial Injury
patterns.criteria: Troponin I >0.04 ng/mL or Troponin T >0.014 ng/mL
patterns.management: URGENT CARDIOLOGY REVIEW. Dual antiplatelet + heparin if ACS confirmed.
